leads.work: Logistics schedulers ask the desk one email at a time for a deal (or a deal extension) whenever gas flows at a meter with no nomination or deal. This covers flow with no deal ticket, deals that expired or failed to roll even though they were flagged evergreen, and evergreen flags left on after a contract ended. The requests get repeated follow-ups.
leads.why: There is a near-identical request every few days: meter 1459, 6879, 1603, 0074, 6387/5192 and 5892, deal 109475, and others. Deals marked evergreen did not roll, so Julie Meyers had to fix them by hand. Aimee Lannou chased meter 6387 at least three times (10/26, 11/1, 11/9). A report that matched meter flow against active deals could catch these automatically.

leads.work: Settlements and accounting staff look into price and volume mismatches between Sitara and counterparty invoices: the wrong index price pulled, demand charges, deals entered twice, deals booked on the wrong meter, manual checks, and suspended payments.
leads.why: Examples include Duke at WAHA (the system pulled $3.95 instead of $2.95, chased several times), the Agave crude price calculation, Metropolitan demand charge entered twice, the Eastman demand charge entered by hand every month, North Shore tier pricing, NWPL price missing in Unify, the Duke deal on the wrong meter two months running, and Ocean Energy suspense. Mary Poorman notes that manual checks are being cut for deals entered wrongly.

leads.work: Risk staff link deal numbers between systems by hand: Tagg, Sitara, SCI and EnronOnline. People keep asking for cross-references, and the links are often missing.
leads.why: Giron repeatedly reminds Radous to link Tagg, Sitara, SCI and EOL numbers. Doug Nelson asks for the Sitara numbers behind Tagg deals. Others ask for tickets or Sitara numbers so they can pay invoices. The origination amount did not come through from the ticket. Linking these numbers automatically would remove this work.

leads.work: Deals with ECC (Canada) counterparties land in the wrong Houston books, including EOL auto-booked deals. Each month before NYMEX invoicing, they have to be found and moved to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by hand.
leads.why: Stacey Vallejo sends reminders every month (October, December and later) listing deal IDs to move. The emails pass through Gossett and Giron to the book admins. A booking rule or validation could prevent the mistake in the first place.

leads.work: Settlements has no reliable way to learn about new book codes or newly active books before running the monthly NYMEX invoices, so someone phones Risk each month to ask.
leads.why: Rebecca Ford found 4 books on her own and set up a monthly calling procedure. Beatrice Reyna asks again each month and chases who has replaced whom.

leads.work: Creating new books, regions, curves and counterparties means emailing several administrators: Tagg, Sitara, CPR, the book request form, curve mapping and trade zones.
leads.why: For Enovate alone, Giron emailed Gary Stadler, Susan Trevino, Regina Perkins, Scott Mills and Jeremy Wong. He sends repeated 'Book Request' forms and asks for curve additions and trade zone mappings, often marked urgent. Book moves also go through Jeremy Wong. One intake workflow could handle all of this.

leads.work: Book admins must mark every book official each night. Missed books end up on a daily exception list reviewed by Sally Beck and Rick Buy. Teams built their own macros to check which books were done.
leads.why: Moscoso reported books not marked official. The control missed books with no net position. Dutch Quigley and Greg Couch passed around and changed a PostID macro. This nightly manual step is a candidate for automation.

leads.work: At month-end roll-off, basis positions have to be calculated twice, once for the TDS download and once for VaR, by marking the book official, unmarking it and recalculating.
leads.why: Gossett says 'Again this month' you will have to calculate twice, which shows it is a recurring manual workaround.

leads.work: Book admins must compact the WeaponX Access database by hand every week because it grows very large (520MB down to 30MB after compacting).
leads.why: This weekly manual maintenance could be scheduled to run automatically.

leads.work: Policy requires a before-and-after minibook for every deal change, and every top-level adjustment needs Lavorato's approval. Both add manual overhead.
leads.why: These are new manual controls. Mini-book access had to be requested and runs on the controller's machine. Gas Daily four-leg deals must also be entered in a fixed leg order so confirms don't fail, which a validation could enforce.

leads.work: Rebuilding the Chicago/Enovate hub deals: Tagg bookings do not match the counterparty spreadsheet, so they have to be reconciled by hand.
leads.why: Over several weeks Giron could not tie the deals out and chased Richman, Radous and Mixon. In the end he chose to start over.

leads.work: Building the yearly budget by hand: Diane Cook collects staffing, salary, training and other items from each manager through spreadsheets and repeated reminders.
leads.why: There were several resends and 'BUDGET HELP' emails. Managers don't know their staff's salaries, so Cook estimates from averages, and she keeps a list of items people forget each year. HR and payroll data could fill much of this in.

leads.work: The monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) hours survey: managers allocate staff hours to activity codes, with reminders and follow-ups.
leads.why: It recurs every month, needed an Access rollout, and comes with deadline reminders. Daren could not use Access and sent a spreadsheet, and Suzanne then followed up with clarifying questions. The OPM team also mentions automating 'driver information'.

leads.work: Each month, controllers write explanations for volume changes over 10% between periods, for Investor Relations.
leads.why: 'It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations'. This has been made monthly and is gathered by email.

leads.work: Meter outages and maintenance notices, plus meter replacement steps, are sent by email to large distribution lists. A meter replacement takes a five-step hand-off across teams, with phone calls after each step.
leads.why: PG&E maintenance notices, the DEFS shut-in, and the new meter 0439. Clem's step-by-step process notes that facility changes 'can not be done automatically' in POPS.

leads.work: Usage tickets can only cover about 3 months each, so a back-dated fix needed 7 separate tickets. Write-offs need a formal letter and deal tickets entered by hand in MOPS.
leads.why: A system limit is forcing duplicated manual entry.

leads.work: Following up on imbalances and payback with pipelines across many contracts that could be netted, and fixing imbalance reports that are poor quality.
leads.why: Gottlob lists dozens of open imbalance and contract-netting questions. He says the imbalance report's columns don't add up and it is missing data. He also asks for a priority curtailment list for the RRC to be pulled from the contract system.

leads.work: Monetized deal tracking: a deal number changed when a book was renamed, which broke the monetization waterfall, and staff had to investigate by hand.
leads.why: There was a $971K shortfall and coordinators were not trained on monetizations.

leads.work: Monthly first-of-month nominations and volume notices from plants and producers (Methanol/MTBE, Swift, Forest Oil) arrive as emails and are keyed in by hand.
leads.why: These are recurring monthly emails with revisions.

leads.work: Requests to approve access and security: SRRS approvals for TDS, Exceed and Sitara access, and gathering contact lists by email.
leads.why: TDS security approval is being handed to the desk controllers, alongside repeated access requests and contact-list collection.

leads.work: Mass forwarding of personal and joke emails with large video attachments (MPG/AVI/EXE) through corporate mail.
leads.why: Giron's sent folder is mostly forwards of multi-megabyte files, which costs time and mailbox storage.

leads.work: Internal audit asks for P&L support (top sheets and curve shift reports), and the requests are passed on to book admins by hand.
leads.why: This was the second request for the August P&L. It could become a standard report package.
